text:
It roams free in the furrow, beats its wing in the wind,
pulses alive in the sun and clings to the pine grove.
You cannot forget it as you would an evil thought:
you will have to listen to it!


It speaks a tongue of bronze and a bird's tongue,
timid pleas, the sea's commands.
You cannot put on a bold face, a solemn frown:
you will have to shelter it!


It bears the airs of a master; excuses cannot soften it.
It shatters flower-cups, cleaves the deep glacier.
You cannot tell it you refuse to harbor it:
you will have to shelter it!


It has subtle tricks in its clever replies,
a scholar's arguments, but in a woman's voice.
Human knowledge may save you, but not divine knowledge:
you will have to believe it!


It ties a linen blindfold on you; you let it stay.
It offers its warm arm; you cannot flee it.
It starts walking, and you follow, spellbound, though you know
this road ends in death!

translation.title: I Love, Love
